notes: The circuit image is the authority; the schematic shows pin 2 but the text and breadboard image use pin 4, so pin 4 is used.

The breadboard image is drawn with rows f-j in the upper half and a-e in the lower half. The catalogue puts rows a-e in bank 't'. The lower half of the image is therefore mapped to bank 't' and the upper half to bank 'b'.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap. Side 1 is column 6 (1.l at 6b.f, 1.r at 6t.e) and side 2 is column 8 (2.l at 8b.f, 2.r at 8t.e).
The pin 4 wire and the resistor's top leg are both in column 6. The short red wire is in column 8 and runs to the lower + rail.

The lower rails are mapped as bottom-row negative = 'bn' and + = 'bp'. The exact rail hole numbers (bp.2, bp.6, bn.1, bn.5) are estimated from the picture. Any hole on the same rail is electrically equivalent.
The resistor is 10 kΩ, set as value=10000. It acts as a pull-down from pin 4 to GND.
The USB cable to the computer is not drawn in the circuit image, so it is not included.
